title: Meta app id and secret pair placeholders, masked secret and derived appsecret_proof
summary: An app-id-and-secret access_token with the documented request template, environment references or a masked secret, the generation call with a placeholder secret, a request that carries an appsecret_proof derived value, and prose that names the parameter.
rationale: A template, an environment reference, a masked display and an angle placeholder stand in for a value kept elsewhere and carry no secret. The appsecret_proof is documented as a sha256 hash of an access token keyed with the app secret: it is a value derived from the secret, not the secret, and the access token it protects is a template here. A client or app ID next to a placeholder secret is an identifier. Flagging any of these would redact documentation and signed-request parameters a reader needs. The case decides nothing about whether the derived proof is itself confidential, only that it is not the app secret.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#244). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: these inputs hold no app secret value. That a placeholder, reference or masked display is not a value, that the derived appsecret_proof is not the app secret and that an app ID is not part of the secret span are the project's decisions; Meta documents the template, the proof derivation and the pair form (carrier existence and derivation only).

sources.supports: The app secret proof is a sha256 hash of your access token, using your app secret as the key.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
